hero.headline: Anthropic raises $65 billion, nears $1 trillion valuation ahead of IPO
hero.body:
Anthropic has closed a $65 billion Series H funding round at a $965 billion post-money valuation, marking what could be the artificial intelligence startup's final private fundraise before a highly anticipated initial public offering.

The funding round represents one of the largest private capital raises in technology history. The valuation places Anthropic among the most valuable private companies globally, approaching the trillion-dollar threshold that only a handful of public companies have reached.

The Series H round comes as Anthropic prepares for a public market debut. The company has not disclosed a specific timeline for the IPO, but the size and valuation of this round suggest the startup is positioning itself for a transition to public markets in the near term.

Anthropic develops large language models and AI safety research. The company competes with OpenAI, Google, and other major players in the artificial intelligence sector. Its flagship product, Claude, serves as a conversational AI assistant for businesses and individual users.

The funding round reflects continued investor appetite for AI companies despite broader market volatility. Venture capital and private equity firms have poured hundreds of billions of dollars into AI startups over the past two years, betting that the technology will transform industries ranging from healthcare to finance.

The $965 billion valuation values Anthropic higher than most Fortune 500 companies. Only a small number of public technology firms, including Apple, Microsoft, and Nvidia, maintain valuations above $1 trillion. Reaching that threshold as a private company would be unprecedented in recent technology history.

Anthropic has raised multiple funding rounds over the past three years as it scales its AI research and product development. The company employs hundreds of researchers and engineers focused on building what it describes as safe and beneficial AI systems.

The impending IPO would provide public market investors their first opportunity to buy shares in Anthropic. The offering could test investor demand for AI companies at elevated valuations, particularly as questions persist about the long-term profitability and competitive dynamics of the sector.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran reach tentative deal to extend ceasefire and reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
U.S. and Iranian negotiators have reached a tentative agreement that could extend their ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, according to U.S. officials. The framework still requires final approval from President Trump before it can take effect.

The emerging arrangement would establish a 60-day ceasefire extension during which several key provisions would take hold. Iran would be permitted to freely sell oil, and the Strait of Hormuz would reopen for international shipping. Iran has agreed to clear mines it deployed in the waterway and refrain from imposing tolls on passing vessels. In return, the U.S. would lift its blockade on Iranian ports that has been in place since April 13.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the potential outcome as achieving "a completely open" Strait of Hormuz "without tolls" if the deal succeeds. However, Iranian media has reported that the strait would remain under Iranian control.

The agreement would also include talks on limiting Iran's nuclear program and would reportedly unfreeze some Iranian assets held in banks outside the country. Hostilities would be halted across all fronts, including between Israel and Lebanon.

Senior Iranian sources told Reuters that Tehran has not agreed to surrender its highly enriched uranium stockpile, and that Iran's nuclear issues were not part of the preliminary agreement. The arrangement reportedly does not address Iran's ballistic missile program or its support for regional allies including Hezbollah in Lebanon and the Houthis in Yemen.

The tentative deal comes as both sides appear to be stepping back from further military escalation. Despite recent exchanges of military strikes between the two nations, neither government has demonstrated interest in resuming full-scale conflict.

Oil markets reacted positively to news of the potential agreement, with prices declining as traders anticipated reduced regional tensions. The Strait of Hormuz is crucial for global oil shipments and handles a significant portion of the world's petroleum traffic.

Trump has shared a draft version of the peace agreement with Israel and other U.S. allies as he reviews the details. The administration is consulting with regional partners before making a final determination on whether to approve the framework.

The agreement represents a potential turning point in the conflict that has seen both countries exchange military strikes in recent weeks. The current ceasefire has remained in place despite accusations from both sides regarding alleged violations of its terms.

U.S. officials involved in the negotiations say the deal addresses immediate concerns about maritime access while establishing a foundation for broader discussions between the two governments. The timing of Trump's decision on whether to approve the arrangement remains unclear.

cards.headline: Netanyahu orders Israeli military to seize 70% of Gaza Strip
cards.teaser: The Israeli prime minister directed his military to take control of most of the Gaza Strip in apparent violation of an existing ceasefire agreement.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has directed the Israeli military to take control of 70 percent of the Gaza Strip, according to reports from The Guardian and CNN. The order appears to conflict with an existing ceasefire agreement.

The directive marks a significant escalation in military operations. It comes as Hamas announced that Mohammed Odeh, the newly appointed head of its military wing, was killed in an Israeli strike on a residential building in Gaza City, along with his wife and two children.

cards.headline: Supreme Court sides with death row inmate who alleged racial bias in jury selection
cards.body:
The US Supreme Court ruled Thursday in favor of Terry Pitchford, a Black man on death row in Mississippi who challenged his capital murder conviction based on racial discrimination during jury selection. The justices voted 5-4 in his favor.

Pitchford was 18 years old when he and another teenager robbed a grocery store in 2004. The other teen, who fired the fatal shots, was a minor and therefore ineligible for the death penalty. Pitchford, now 40, was convicted of capital murder and sentenced to death.

The central issue in the Supreme Court case involved jury selection. Prosecutors removed four of the five Black jurors from the pool, resulting in a jury of 11 white jurors and one Black juror that convicted Pitchford and imposed his death sentence. The prosecutor, Doug Evans, who had a documented history of dismissing Black jurors for discriminatory reasons, made the strikes.

Pitchford's attorney objected to the strikes during trial, but Judge Joseph Loper allowed them to stand. In his majority opinion, Justice Brett Kavanaugh wrote that "the trial court did not afford Pitchford's counsel a sufficient opportunity to rebut the prosecutor's proffered race-neutral reasons for striking the four Black jurors and never determined whether the prosecutor's stated reasons were pretextual."

The Supreme Court's decision reinstated a federal judge's earlier ruling that had invalidated Pitchford's conviction. That federal ruling found his attorney was prevented from questioning whether Evans's jury selection decisions were based on race.

The case centered on application of the Batson challenge, a legal framework established by the Supreme Court in 1986 through Batson v. Kentucky. The Batson challenge creates a three-step process for addressing potential racial discrimination in jury selection. First, the objecting party must demonstrate an inference of discrimination. Second, the striking party must provide race-neutral explanations for removing specific jurors. Third, the judge must determine whether purposeful discrimination occurred.

Much of the oral arguments focused on Judge Loper's handling of the third step of this process. The case parallels a similar situation from seven years ago involving the same judge and prosecutor. In that case, the Supreme Court overturned the death sentence and conviction of Curtis Flowers, another Black man who had been tried six times over more than 20 years. At that time, Justice Kavanaugh wrote that Evans showed a "relentless, determined effort to rid the jury of Black individuals."

The Supreme Court's decision provides Pitchford with a pathway to challenge his conviction. Prosecutors may seek to retry him, but the ruling reinforces constitutional protections designed to prevent racial bias in jury selection and ensure fair trials in capital cases.

cards.headline: Judge declines to block Trump executive order limiting mail-in voting
cards.teaser: A federal judge refused to immediately halt changes to mail-in voting procedures ordered by the president.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C., has declined to temporarily block President Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting. The decision allows the order to remain in effect while legal challenges proceed.

Democrats had requested an immediate injunction to stop the order's implementation. Another judge may rule on the matter soon.

cards.headline: Guatemala agrees to joint anti-gang operations with U.S.
cards.teaser: The agreement allows joint military operations inside Guatemala as part of the Trump administration's expanding campaign in Latin America.
cards.body:
Guatemala has agreed to allow joint operations with the United States to strike drug gangs operating within its borders. The deal represents an expansion of the Trump administration's military engagement in Latin America.

The agreement is part of a broader push by the Trump administration to secure cooperation from Latin American countries for joint operations inside their territories. The administration has been pressing multiple countries in the region to accept similar arrangements targeting criminal organizations.

cards.headline: About 8 percent of Americans lacked health insurance in 2025
cards.teaser: The CDC reported the uninsured rate remained largely unchanged from 2024, though the total number of uninsured people grew by about 800,000.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

About 8 percent of the US population was uninsured in 2025, according to estimates from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The overall percentage was largely unchanged from 2024.

The number of uninsured people grew by about 800,000, including 300,000 children. The uninsured rate remains lower than it was in 2019, according to the CDC's National Health Interview Survey.

---

Reason: The additional source material provided (BBC articles about oil prices and Gaza) concerns different stories unrelated to US health insurance coverage. Therefore, the original card text is returned unchanged.

cards.headline: Israel conducts targeted strike on Beirut
cards.teaser: Israeli forces struck the Lebanese capital, which had largely avoided attacks even as Israel and Hezbollah accused each other of ceasefire violations.
cards.body:
Israel carried out a targeted strike on Beirut, marking a significant escalation in the Lebanese capital. The city had been largely spared from direct attacks despite ongoing tensions between the two sides.

The strike occurred amid accusations from both Israel and Hezbollah that each had broken the ceasefire agreement reached the previous month.

cards.headline: 16 students die in Kenya school fire
cards.teaser: The deaths occurred as questions emerged about school safety standards following another deadly fire at a Kenyan educational facility.
cards.body:
A fire swept through a dormitory at Utumishi girls academy in Gilgil, Nakuru county, killing at least 16 students. The blaze erupted just after midnight at the school, located about 76 miles northwest of Nairobi in Kenya's Rift Valley.

The incident left parents in an anxious wait for updates on their children, with many still seeking information hours after the fire broke out. The disaster has raised fresh concerns about safety standards at educational institutions across Kenya.

cards.headline: Guatemala agrees to joint anti-gang operations with U.S.
cards.teaser: The agreement allows joint military operations inside Guatemala as part of the Trump administration's expanding campaign in Latin America.
cards.body:
Guatemala has agreed to allow joint operations with the United States to strike drug gangs operating within its borders. The deal represents an expansion of the Trump administration's military engagement in Latin America.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: The investigation centers on whether the former columnist lied about funding she received for her civil lawsuit against President Trump.
cards.body:
The U.S. Justice Department has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, the former columnist who won civil lawsuits against President Trump. The investigation examines whether Carroll made false statements regarding the funding she received for her civil case against the president.

Carroll previously succeeded in civil court proceedings against Trump before his return to the presidency. The Justice Department is now scrutinizing the financial sources that supported her legal action.

cards.headline: U.S. re-sanctions U.N. expert critical of Israel
cards.teaser: The Treasury Department reinstated penalties on Francesca Albanese just days after a court ordered the sanctions suspended.
cards.body:
The United States has re-imposed sanctions on Francesca Albanese, a United Nations legal expert whose work on Israel has drawn accusations of antisemitism. The move comes days after a U.S. court ordered the Treasury Department to suspend its penalties against her.

Albanese's work at the United Nations focusing on Israel has generated controversy and led to the initial sanctions. The Treasury Department has now reinstated those penalties despite the recent court order.

cards.headline: US and Iran reach tentative deal to extend ceasefire and begin nuclear talks
cards.teaser: The framework would extend a ceasefire and launch nuclear negotiations, though it awaits presidential approval.
cards.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement on a framework to extend their current ceasefire and initiate nuclear negotiations. According to US officials, the deal remains subject to President Trump's approval before moving forward.

The agreement signals a potential diplomatic shift between the two countries on nuclear matters that have long strained their relationship. The framework would combine an immediate extension of the ceasefire with talks aimed at addressing Iran's nuclear program.

cards.headline: Former senior CIA officer accused of taking gold bars and millions in cash
cards.teaser: David Rush faces charges of theft and false statements after FBI agents found gold and cash in his Virginia home.
cards.body:
David Rush, a former senior CIA officer, has been charged with theft and making false statements. Investigators discovered gold bars and millions in cash in his Virginia home that had gone missing from a CIA storage space.

The FBI alleges that Rush took the valuables while employed at the agency. Prosecutors also accuse him of lying to investigators about the missing items.

cards.headline: Judge declines to block Trump executive order limiting mail-in voting
cards.teaser: A federal judge refused to immediately halt changes to mail-in voting procedures ordered by the president.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C., has declined to temporarily block President Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting. The decision allows the order to remain in effect while legal challenges proceed.

Democrats had requested an immediate injunction to stop the order's implementation. Another judge may rule on the matter soon.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary endorses proposal for $250 bill featuring Trump
cards.teaser: Scott Bessent confirmed limited steps toward creating a new denomination with the president's portrait.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has endorsed a proposal to create a $250 bill featuring President Trump's portrait. Trump appointees at the Treasury Department are advancing the plan.

However, federal law currently prohibits printing images of living people on US currency. Trump allies in Congress are working to pass legislation that would create an exception to this rule, allowing the new denomination to move forward.

cards.headline: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer will not seek presidency in 2028
cards.teaser: The Democratic governor announced she will not run for president in the next election cycle.
cards.body:
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer said she will not run for president in 2028. The Democratic governor's announcement removes a potential candidate from the field as party members begin positioning for the next presidential race.

Whitmer has been considered a rising figure in Democratic politics and her decision leaves the 2028 field more open. She did not provide detailed reasons for her decision in the available reports.

cards.headline: Trump refiles $10 billion defamation lawsuit against Wall Street Journal
cards.teaser: The president submitted a revised lawsuit over a report about alleged ties to Jeffrey Epstein.
cards.body:
President Trump's legal team has refiled a $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and its publisher Dow Jones after a Florida judge dismissed the original case last month. The suit challenges a WSJ story from 2003 alleging that Trump sent a "bawdy" letter to financier Jeffrey Epstein.

The case marks a significant legal clash between Trump and Rupert Murdoch, who owns the Wall Street Journal. Trump claims the newspaper's reporting damaged his reputation by describing the letter and suggesting connections between him and Epstein.

hero.headline: Treasury launches Trump Accounts app to manage $1,000 federal investment for each child
hero.body:
The US Treasury rolled out a new mobile application to manage federally funded investment accounts that provide $1,000 for each American child. The Trump Accounts app launched nationwide, allowing parents and guardians to access and monitor the accounts.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed the app's release. The program creates individual investment accounts funded by the federal government, with each child receiving an initial $1,000 deposit.

The application allows account holders to view balances and track the performance of their investments. Parents and guardians can download the app to manage accounts on behalf of their children.

The Treasury Department did not specify how many children qualify for the program or what investment options the accounts include. The launch represents a new federal initiative to provide direct financial support to American families through individually managed investment vehicles.

The program appears designed to give children a financial foundation through government-funded accounts that can grow over time. Account holders will use the mobile app as the primary interface for monitoring and managing the funds.

Multiple news outlets confirmed the app's launch, with coverage noting the Treasury Department's role in administering the program. The initiative marks a departure from traditional federal assistance programs by creating individual investment accounts rather than direct payments or benefits.

cards.headline: Anthropic surpasses OpenAI as most valuable AI startup with $965 billion valuation
cards.teaser: The artificial intelligence company raised $65 billion in new funding, giving it a post-money valuation that exceeds OpenAI's worth.
cards.body:
Anthropic closed a $65 billion Series H funding round, achieving a $965 billion post-money valuation. This positions the AI startup as the most valuable private AI company, surpassing OpenAI.

The funding round brings Anthropic's valuation close to $1 trillion. The company is reportedly preparing for an initial public offering, making this Series H round potentially its final private fundraise before going public.

cards.headline: Tilman Fertitta to acquire Caesars Entertainment in $17.6 billion deal
cards.teaser: The billionaire businessman reached an agreement to buy the Las Vegas Strip casino operator for approximately $6 billion in equity value.
cards.body:
Businessman Tilman Fertitta is acquiring Caesars Entertainment in a deal valued at $17.6 billion including debt. The casino operator's equity is valued at approximately $6 billion.

Fertitta's acquisition includes multiple properties on the Las Vegas Strip. The transaction raises questions about how customer loyalty programs and player rewards will be managed under new ownership.

cards.headline: Google engineer charged with using internal data to make $1.2 million on prediction markets
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors allege the employee accessed confidential search data to place winning bets on Polymarket.
cards.body:
The US Justice Department has charged Michele Spagnuolo, a 36-year-old Italian citizen and Google software engineer, with using insider information to place bets on Polymarket. Prosecutors allege he leveraged confidential data about Google's most-searched list to make wagers on the prediction market platform, earning $1.2 million in profits.

The case represents another instance of alleged insider trading on Polymarket. Last month, prosecutors charged a US Army soldier with using classified information to place bets about military action in Venezuela on the same platform.

cards.headline: CVS restores coverage for Eli Lilly obesity drug Zepbound after customer complaints
cards.teaser: The pharmacy benefit manager reversed its decision to drop the weight loss medication from its formulary.
cards.body:
CVS Caremark has restored coverage for Zepbound, Eli Lilly's obesity treatment, following customer complaints about its removal from the pharmacy benefit manager's drug plans. The reversal means millions of Americans with CVS insurance can again access the medication.

The expanded coverage also includes Eli Lilly's oral obesity pill. The decision to reinstate Zepbound coverage boosted Eli Lilly's market value back to the $1 trillion mark, reflecting improved commercial prospects for the drug.

cards.headline: Bari Weiss appoints Nick Bilton as executive producer of 60 Minutes
cards.teaser: The CBS editor in chief named the tech journalist to lead the news program and removed two on-air correspondents.
cards.body:
CBS editor in chief Bari Weiss has appointed Nick Bilton, a technology journalist and filmmaker, as executive producer of 60 Minutes. The move represents a significant leadership change for the long-running news program.

The shake-up comes as the network did not renew the contract of veteran correspondent Sharyn Alfonsi for the show's upcoming 59th season. Alfonsi had accused CBS News of penalizing her for refusing to compromise factually accurate reporting, following the network's decision to shelve a segment she reported on a prison in El Salvador.

cards.headline: Stock markets reach new highs as tech companies rally
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq hit record levels, with Snowflake leading gains among technology stocks.
cards.body:
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq climbed to fresh records as technology stocks surged, with Snowflake leading the gains among the sector. The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined as oil prices initially rose before moderating on reports of a potential breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations.

Market participants remained focused on corporate earnings reports, which continued to demonstrate strength across US companies. The mixed performance reflected ongoing attention to geopolitical developments and their potential impact on energy prices.

cards.headline: Hackers target Signal users with phishing attacks to steal message backups
cards.teaser: A hacking campaign is attempting to trick Signal users into revealing secret recovery keys that unlock online message backups.
cards.body:
A new phishing campaign is attempting to trick Signal users into surrendering their secret recovery keys. These keys grant access to online backups containing encrypted copies of past messages.

The recovery keys are particularly valuable because while Signal uses end-to-end encryption for messages, users who enable cloud backups create encrypted archives of their message history. Attackers are using social engineering tactics to compromise Signal accounts through coordinated phishing attempts.

cards.headline: Prison phone service Pay Tel exposes driver's licenses of 300,000 callers
cards.teaser: A security lapse at Pay Tel publicly exposed sensitive ID documents and inmate communications for over 300,000 users.
cards.body:
A security oversight at Pay Tel, which operates pay phone services in prisons, left a database containing sensitive information publicly accessible online. The exposed data included driver's licenses and other identification documents submitted by over 300,000 callers, as well as inmate communications.

Security researchers identified the unprotected database and notified Pay Tel of the vulnerability. The company secured the data following the disclosure.

cards.headline: Corgi doubles valuation to $2.6 billion in three weeks with same investors
cards.teaser: The startup raised $106 million at a valuation double what it commanded just three weeks earlier, both rounds from the same investor group.
cards.body:
Corgi announced a $106 million funding round at a $2.6 billion valuation, exactly double what the company was valued at three weeks prior. The same group of investors participated in both rounds.

The rapid valuation doubling has drawn attention within the startup community. While companies raising consecutive rounds with steep valuation increases have become routine, a valuation that doubles in just three weeks—especially with an identical investor group backing both rounds—represents an unusual pattern in venture capital.

cards.headline: Bluesky adds long-form content feature
cards.teaser: The social media platform is introducing long-form content capabilities in its latest update.
cards.body:
Bluesky announced it is adding long-form content to its platform in a new update. The feature expands the social media site beyond its current short-form posting format.

The addition positions Bluesky to compete with platforms that offer article-length content. The company framed the update as an alternative to similar features on competitor platforms including X.

cards.headline: Exchanges develop AI token futures as commodity market emerges
cards.teaser: Major exchanges are designing derivative products around AI tokens, treating them as raw materials similar to electricity or bandwidth.
cards.body:
Large exchanges are designing derivative products around AI tokens, viewing them increasingly as raw material inputs comparable to electricity or bandwidth rather than purely computational outputs. This shift reflects growing recognition of AI tokens as tradable commodities in financial markets.

The move toward AI token futures contracts follows rising demand for standardized trading mechanisms. The financial products allow market participants to trade AI tokens through exchange-based derivative instruments, similar to established commodity futures for traditional resources.

cards.headline: Healthcare software company H1 raises $40 million from CVS
cards.teaser: The funding demonstrates that software-as-a-service startups can still attract investment despite AI competition.
cards.body:
H1 has secured $40 million in funding from CVS Health. The investment demonstrates that software-as-a-service startups continue to attract capital despite growing competition from AI tools.

CEO Ariel Katz emphasized that while artificial intelligence can automate workflow tasks similar to traditional SaaS platforms, H1's proprietary dataset of doctor information provides a defensible advantage. This unique data collection differentiates the company from AI systems that lack access to the same information resources.

hero.headline: Stanley Cup champion Claude Lemieux dies at 60
hero.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup champion known for his playoff performances, has died at 60. According to TMZ, Lemieux died by suicide.

Lemieux won Stanley Cups with three different teams during his NHL career. He captured championships with the Montreal Canadiens, New Jersey Devils, and Colorado Avalanche. His playoff intensity and competitive style defined his reputation across nearly two decades in professional hockey.

The NHL and multiple sports outlets confirmed his death. Lemieux's 1996 Stanley Cup victory with Colorado marked one of four championship runs during his career. He built a reputation as a fierce competitor particularly effective in postseason play.

Lemieux played forward and became known for his physical style and ability to elevate his game during the playoffs. His career spanned multiple teams, but his championship success with New Jersey and Colorado remained his most notable achievements.

The hockey community mourned the loss of a player who contributed to multiple championship teams. Lemieux's four Stanley Cup rings placed him among a select group of players who won multiple championships with different organizations.

His death marks the loss of one of hockey's notable playoff performers from the 1980s and 1990s. Lemieux's competitive approach and championship pedigree made him a recognizable figure in NHL history. The circumstances of his death bring attention to mental health challenges that can affect athletes at any stage of life.

Details about services or survivors were not immediately available. The NHL community recognized Lemieux's contributions to the sport and his role on multiple championship teams throughout his playing career.

cards.headline: World number one Jannik Sinner loses in second round at French Open
cards.teaser: Top-ranked tennis player Jannik Sinner suffered a second-round defeat to Juan Manuel Cerundolo at the French Open.
cards.body:
Jannik Sinner, the world number one, suffered a shock second-round defeat at the French Open, losing to Argentina's Juan Manuel Cerúndolo 3-6, 2-6, 7-5, 6-1, 6-1. Sinner described the loss as "tough to accept" given his current form and ranking.

The Italian attributed his poor performance to illness rather than the extreme heat at Roland Garros. After the defeat, Sinner said he needed time to recover both physically and mentally, indicating he would likely skip grass-court tournaments before Wimbledon to prepare for his return.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey investigate FIFA over World Cup ticket pricing
cards.teaser: Attorneys general from New York and New Jersey have subpoenaed FIFA over ticket sales practices for the upcoming World Cup.
cards.body:
New York and New Jersey authorities are investigating FIFA over its World Cup ticket sales practices. The attorneys general from both states have issued subpoenas after fans reported being misled about ticket availability and seat locations.

The probe follows widespread outrage over soaring ticket prices for the 2026 tournament. While FIFA's ticketing system has historically operated without major controversy, the significant price increases this cycle prompted complaints from prospective attendees in the two states hosting multiple World Cup matches.

cards.headline: Serena Williams in talks for potential return at Queen's Club
cards.teaser: Serena Williams is discussing a possible return to competitive tennis at Queen's Club next month.
cards.body:
Serena Williams is considering a competitive return to tennis at Queen's Club in London next month at age 44. The 23-time Grand Slam champion has been reinstated in the drug testing pool for six months, clearing the way for her comeback. She last competed in 2022.

Williams is seeking a doubles wildcard at the Queen's WTA 500 event, which begins on June 8, to partner with 19-year-old Canadian Victoria Mboko, who is ranked No. 19 in singles.

cards.headline: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart addresses team after Trump introduction
cards.teaser: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart spoke to teammates during a team meeting following his introduction of President Trump.
cards.body:
Jaxson Dart addressed the New York Giants during a team meeting to discuss his introduction of President Trump. Multiple sources confirmed that Dart spoke to the locker room about the political rally appearance.

Rookie Abdul Carter was not present for the Giants team meeting. NFL Network and ESPN reported that Dart's address to teammates followed controversy over his participation in the Trump event. The quarterback met with the team to discuss the situation.

cards.headline: US coach Mauricio Pochettino holds talks with AC Milan
cards.teaser: United States national team manager Mauricio Pochettino has held initial discussions with AC Milan about becoming their next manager.
cards.body:
Mauricio Pochettino has held initial talks with AC Milan about becoming their next manager. The discussions come after the Serie A club sacked Massimiliano Allegri from the position.

Pochettino currently serves as head coach of the United States men's national soccer team. The talks suggest Milan is considering him for the role next season as they search for a replacement manager.

cards.headline: Arizona's Koa Peat to stay in NBA draft
cards.teaser: Arizona star Koa Peat will remain in the 2026 NBA draft rather than return to college basketball.
cards.body:
Koa Peat has decided to stay in the 2026 NBA draft, according to sources. The Arizona player will not withdraw his name before the deadline, ending his college basketball career.

The withdrawal deadline prompted multiple decisions from college players weighing their NBA prospects. Peat's choice means Arizona will need to replace one of its stars ahead of next season. Multiple outlets released rankings and analysis of returning college basketball players following the deadline for draft withdrawal decisions.

hero.headline: Artists Drop Out of Freedom 250 Concert Series After Being Listed on Lineup
hero.body:
Several musicians have withdrawn from a concert series planned for America's 250th anniversary after finding themselves announced on the lineup without their consent. The event, called Freedom 250, is scheduled to take place on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., and has drawn immediate backlash from performers who say they never agreed to participate.

Morris Day declined involvement, stating it was a "no." Young MC also dropped out of the series. Freedom Williams of C + C Music Factory posted an expletive-filled statement rejecting his inclusion. Milli Vanilli similarly denied any participation in the Trump-linked event.

In contrast, Vanilla Ice indicated he would perform at the concerts, which are part of celebrations marking the nation's semiquicentennial anniversary.

The concert series announcement generated swift pushback from several performers who discovered they had been listed without confirmed participation. Artists began making public statements to distance themselves from the event shortly after the lineup was made public, creating confusion about which acts had actually committed to appearing.

The Freedom 250 concerts represent one component of planned observances for America's 250th birthday. The event's connection to the former president appears to have influenced some artists' decisions to withdraw or clarify their non-involvement in the anniversary celebration.

The National Mall in Washington serves as the planned venue for the concert series, a historic location that has hosted numerous national celebrations and public gatherings throughout American history.

Organizers have not publicly addressed the withdrawals or explained the circumstances surrounding how artists came to be listed on promotional materials without confirmed commitments. The announcement of the initial lineup preceded the wave of denials and dropouts by a short period, creating questions about the planning process and communication between organizers and performers.

The rapid series of public rejections highlights concerns some artists have about being associated with the event. Rather than remaining silent after being announced, multiple performers felt compelled to actively deny their involvement through direct statements to the media and public.

This situation underscores how artists carefully manage their public associations and the potential reputational risks of being linked to politically contentious events. The Freedom 250 concert series, intended to celebrate an important national milestone, has instead become marked by controversy and public disputes over who would actually perform.

As the anniversary celebration moves forward, organizers will need to rebuild their lineup with artists who have explicitly agreed to participate, while managing questions about how the initial announcement was handled.

cards.headline: Lionsgate Sets June 2027 Release for Rambo Prequel
cards.teaser: The studio scheduled John Rambo for theaters between two major franchise releases next summer.
cards.body:
Lionsgate has scheduled John Rambo, a prequel to the action franchise, for a June 4, 2027 theatrical release. The film will arrive during a competitive summer movie season alongside other major studio releases.

The prequel arrives one week after Disney's Star Wars: Starfighter and one week before Sony's Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse and a Warner Bros. Oceans prequel, both set for June 11.

cards.headline: CNN Adds Fourth of July Special with Anderson Cooper and Andy Cohen
cards.teaser: The network plans Independence Eve Live on July 3 with the pair who host its New Year's Eve coverage.
cards.body:
CNN announced a new holiday broadcast featuring Anderson Cooper and Andy Cohen. The special, titled Independence Eve Live with Anderson Andy, will air on July 3.

The two hosts have anchored CNN's New Years Eve coverage from Times Square in recent years. The network is expanding their partnership to include a July Fourth broadcast.

cards.headline: Role Model Announces Third Album for August Release
cards.teaser: The musician set an August 7 date for Chuck Timely & the Hourglass.
cards.body:
Role Model will release a third album titled Chuck Timely & the Hourglass on August 7. The record follows the musician's previous album Kansas Anymore.

The announcement comes as the artist prepares the next chapter in a recording career that has produced two prior full-length releases.

cards.headline: The Testaments Season Finale Explores Agnes and Becka Relationship
cards.teaser: Stars Chase Infiniti and Mattea Conforti discussed a private moment between their characters in the Hulu series conclusion.
cards.body:
The first season of Hulu's The Testaments ended with a finale episode titled Secateurs. The Handmaid's Tale sequel series featured what stars Chase Infiniti and Mattea Conforti described as a significant private moment between their characters Agnes and Becka.

Conforti characterized Becka as Agnes's person in life. The season finale included what the cast identified as upsetting and shocking moments alongside the character development between the two leads.

cards.headline: M&M Partners with Love Island USA for Eighth Season
cards.teaser: The candy brand released limited-edition packages printed with phrases from the reality show.
cards.body:
M&M became the exclusive confectionery partner for the eighth season of Love Island USA. The company released a limited-edition play-along pack to mark the collaboration.

The special packages contain game boards and custom candy printed with recurring phrases from the show. The printed candy features lines including "Bombshell Arrives" and "Got a Text."

cards.headline: CNBC Hires Ken Brown as Managing Editor for Digital
cards.teaser: The financial journalist will oversee digital editorial operations and strategy starting in June.
cards.body:
CNBC named Ken Brown managing editor of digital and editorial strategy. Brown will report to editor in chief David Cho and begin on June 8.

Brown comes from a background in financial journalism. At CNBC, he will oversee the business news outlet's digital editorial operations and contribute to overall strategy development.

hero.headline: Supreme Court rules in favor of Mississippi death row inmate in racial bias case
hero.body:
The US Supreme Court ruled Thursday in favor of Terry Pitchford, a Black man on death row in Mississippi who challenged his capital murder conviction based on racial bias in jury selection. The justices sided with Pitchford in a 5-4 decision.

Pitchford was 18 years old when he was convicted of murder. For the past two decades, he has fought to overturn his conviction, arguing that Black jurors were improperly excluded from his trial. His legal team contended that the jury selection process was shaped by discriminatory practices that undermined the fairness of the proceedings.

The Supreme Court's decision validates Pitchford's core argument that racial bias influenced how jurors were chosen for his case. The ruling acknowledges that the jury composition was affected by improper exclusion of potential jurors based on their race.

However, the decision does not automatically overturn Pitchford's death sentence. Instead, it confirms the legitimacy of his claims about racial discrimination in the jury selection process and clears the way for further legal proceedings to address the conviction.

The case represents a significant development in Pitchford's long legal battle. Throughout his two decades in the appeals process, he has consistently identified jury selection methods as the central flaw in his trial proceedings. The Supreme Court's ruling now recognizes the validity of these concerns.

This decision could have broader implications for other capital cases where defendants have raised similar challenges to jury selection practices. The ruling establishes an important precedent regarding how courts should evaluate claims of racial bias in the jury selection process.

The path forward for Pitchford will involve additional legal proceedings to determine what remedy should be applied given the court's finding of racial bias in jury selection. Legal experts have noted that such findings can lead to various outcomes, ranging from new trials to resentencing hearings, depending on how lower courts proceed.

The case highlights ongoing concerns about racial discrimination within the American criminal justice system, particularly in capital cases where the stakes are highest. Jury selection has long been identified as an area where racial bias can influence outcomes, and courts have grappled with how to address such discrimination.

Pitchford's case joins a growing body of jurisprudence examining the intersection of race and jury selection in death penalty cases. As the legal system moves forward with the additional proceedings mandated by Thursday's ruling, the case will likely continue to draw attention from civil rights advocates and legal observers interested in fairness and discrimination in criminal trials.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary declines to discuss reported US-Iran agreement
cards.teaser: Scott Bessent avoided questions about a memorandum of understanding between US and Iranian negotiators that President Trump has not formally approved.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent sidestepped questions about a reported memorandum of understanding between US and Iranian negotiators during a White House press briefing. The tentative framework has not yet been approved by President Trump.

According to reports, the agreement would extend the current ceasefire between the two countries and launch nuclear talks. Oil prices dipped following news of the potential deal, with international benchmark Brent crude declining as markets reacted to the prospect of reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

cards.headline: FEMA head says agency prepared for hurricane season
cards.teaser: Acting FEMA administrator Bob Fenton told CBS News the agency is ready for hurricane season as the Trump administration encourages more state involvement in disaster recovery.
cards.body:
Bob Fenton, acting administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, said FEMA is prepared for the upcoming hurricane season. Fenton made the statement during an interview with CBS News.

The reassurance comes as the Trump administration encourages states to take greater responsibility in disaster recovery efforts. Despite this shift in approach to disaster management, Fenton indicated the agency is ready for the challenges ahead.

cards.headline: FBI warns of fake FIFA websites targeting World Cup fans
cards.teaser: The FBI issued a warning about cybercriminals creating fake FIFA websites using similar URLs and designs to trick consumers ahead of the 2026 World Cup.
cards.body:
The FBI issued a warning about malicious cyber actors creating fraudulent websites designed to mimic official FIFA pages ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. These fake sites closely replicate legitimate FIFA features to trick visitors into engaging with them.

The scammers use slightly misspelled web addresses to make their sites appear genuine and more likely to fool unsuspecting fans. The FBI released this alert as public interest in the World Cup grows and ticket sales activity increases.

cards.headline: Vance says military must not allow AI to make life or death decisions
cards.teaser: The vice president told Air Force Academy graduates the military should never let artificial intelligence make life and death decisions.
cards.body:
Vice President Vance addressed Air Force Academy graduates and stated the military should never allow artificial intelligence to make life and death decisions. The speech comes as the Pentagon continues moving forward with incorporating AI into military operations.

Vance's remarks set a boundary on the use of AI in warfare even as the Defense Department expands its AI capabilities. The statement establishes a position on the ethical limits of autonomous technology in combat situations.

cards.headline: Protests planned for Trump's 80th birthday by No Kings movement
cards.teaser: The No Kings movement announced nationwide protests scheduled for June 14, President Trump's 80th birthday.
cards.body:
The No Kings movement has announced nationwide protests scheduled for June 14, marking President Trump's 80th birthday. The organizers frame the demonstrations around America's approaching 250th anniversary, positioning it as a defining moment for the nation's future direction.

According to the movement's messaging, the protests represent a choice between two competing visions for America. The organizers are calling for citizens to participate in shaping the country's next chapter as it approaches its milestone anniversary.

cards.headline: Former New York Times columnist to lead 60 Minutes
cards.teaser: CBS News editor in chief Bari Weiss selected former New York Times technology columnist Nick Bilton to lead 60 Minutes, replacing executive producer Tanya Simon.
cards.body:
Bari Weiss, editor in chief of CBS News, has appointed Nick Bilton, a former New York Times technology columnist, to lead the primetime news broadcast "60 Minutes." Bilton replaces executive producer Tanya Simon in the role.

Weiss praised Bilton as an entrepreneurial journalist well-suited to lead the long-running news magazine. His background in technology journalism brings a new perspective to the program.
